focus_areas.area: Network ACL rules and default deny enforcement
Internet gateway exposure and public routing
Network traffic monitoring and VPC Flow Logs
VPC endpoints and private service access

rule.title: Security Group SSH/RDP Exposure
rule.action: Flag ingress rules allowing SSH/RDP from unrestricted sources

rule.title: Public Internet Gateway
rule.description: IGW existence combined with public subnet routing is Medium (if intended)
rule.action: Verify route tables have appropriate restrictions to IGW

rule.title: Default VPC Usage
rule.description: Using AWS default VPC is Medium risk (should use custom VPC)
rule.action: Check if resources are in default VPC vs. custom VPCs

rule.title: VPC Flow Logs
rule.description: Missing VPC Flow Logs is High risk (no traffic visibility)
rule.action: Verify Flow Logs are enabled and sent to CloudWatch/S3

rule.title: NACL Rules
rule.description: Permissive NACL rules allowing all traffic are Medium risk
rule.action: Check for rules allowing all ports (0-65535) from any source

rule.title: Overpermissive Security Groups
rule.description: Security groups allowing 0.0.0.0/0 for application ports are High risk
rule.action: Identify DB ports (3306, 5432) or app ports exposed to internet

focus.check: Custom application ports with public access
Custom NACLs with gaps in rule coverage
Routes with 0.0.0.0/0 destination and public IGW
Default VPC usage vs. custom VPCs
Gateway endpoints for S3, DynamoDB (should be used)
Interface endpoints for private service access

steps.step: 1. Go to EC2 > Security Groups > [Group Name]
2. Find ingress rule allowing 22 or 3389 from 0.0.0.0/0
3. Edit rule: change source from 0.0.0.0/0 to specific IP or security group
4. If bastion needed, use bastion host with restricted access
5. Consider using Systems Manager Session Manager (no SSH needed)
1. Go to VPC > Your VPCs > [VPC Name]
2. Select Flow Logs tab > Create Flow Log
3. Choose destination: CloudWatch Logs or S3
4. Create IAM role for CloudWatch Logs delivery
5. Enable and monitor for suspicious traffic patterns
1. Identify database security group allowing internet access
2. Remove/restrict ingress rules for database ports
3. Create separate security group for database (restricted)
5. Use VPC endpoints or private connectivity for access
